findings.summary: out/raw is never cleared before writing, so state.csv files from modules removed or renamed since an earlier run persist and are counted by the S4 raw tally while data.json no longer contains them.
findings.effect: After an upstream module disappears, the INTERNAL_AVAILABILITY acceptance check fails (or compares against stale data) on a rerun into the same out directory.

findings.summary: accessor_to_path only inserts a hyphen before each capital, so Gradle accessors for directories containing digits or acronym runs (e.g. mapDisplay3d, mapDisplayUI) map to the wrong path and the api dependency is silently dropped by the in_scope filter.
findings.effect: A transitive consumer (via an api dependency) is missing from the dashboard with no warning, understating that artifact's consumer total.

findings.summary: KEY_RE token class is [A-Za-z0-9_-] only, so a key containing other characters (. / + % etc.) is cut at the first such character and the remainder stays in the output as key=*** followed by the rest of the secret.
findings.effect: Part of an API key can still appear in dashboard.html or data.json when the key contains a character outside the class.

findings.summary: setdefault dedupes by module keeping the first alias even when its version resolved to None (missing ref or rich version), so a later alias with a resolvable version is discarded.
findings.effect: A consumer can show no pinned version for a library, or be left out of the lowest-pin computation, although another alias of the same module declares a version.

findings.summary: Libraries declared with group/name keys instead of module (valid in a version catalog) are skipped without any error, so such direct pairs vanish silently.
findings.effect: A consumer using the group/name form shows fewer or zero consumed artifacts and the dashboard reports it as a valid result.

findings.summary: Lines with fewer than 7 ';'-separated fields are dropped silently in parse_rows, so a malformed or truncated state.csv row is neither counted nor reported.
findings.effect: Stability counts for a package can be lower than the real number of API rows without any warning.

findings.summary: Any HTTP 404 (including a missing CODEOWNERS or a mistyped path) returns None; collect then passes None to Codeowners, which calls .splitlines() on it and fails with an unrelated AttributeError.
findings.effect: A missing CODEOWNERS file stops the run with a confusing traceback instead of a clear error naming the missing file.

merged.summary: Redaction responsibility is scattered: the transport layer (github.raw) redacts, build.collect redacts extra catalogs, __main__ redacts data.json and html.render redacts again, so no single stage owns M5 and a new output path can silently skip it.

findings.summary: Raw state files are written into out/raw/ without clearing earlier runs; test_acceptance's S4 check os.walk()s the whole out/raw and compares its tally to the model's state_totals, so a module removed or unpublished since a previous run leaves stale state.csv files that the new model no longer counts.
findings.effect: After the SDK drops a module, the S4 acceptance check reports a mismatch (or passes against stale data) even though the fresh dashboard is correct.

merged.summary: The CLI builds the out/raw/<module>/api/state.csv layout using build.STATE_FILE, so the on-disk layout that acceptance tests read is split between __main__ and build instead of one writer owning output paths.

findings.summary: github.raw is documented to return None on 404, but gradle_texts values and the CODEOWNERS text (line 306) are passed straight to parse_module/Codeowners, which assume str; a None build file or CODEOWNERS crashes with TypeError/AttributeError instead of a clear error (catalogs get an explicit None check at line 327, these do not).
findings.effect: If a build file or CODEOWNERS is missing or moved, the generator dies with an opaque traceback rather than a message naming the missing file.

findings.summary: _packages returns rows whose second element is either a counts dict or a sentinel string (STATE_UNKNOWN / EMPTY_CELL) and _package_sections discriminates with isinstance(counts, str); presentation state is encoded in the data type and inferred from empty packages/None stability instead of an explicit model field.

The model shape consumed by html.render is documented only in the html.py docstring while build.assemble builds the dict inline; the two modules share an implicit untyped contract, so a renamed key in build fails only at render time (html uses .get defaults that mask omissions).
findings.effect: A key rename in the model could silently render an empty section in the dashboard rather than failing.

findings.summary: KEY_RE only matches lowercase `key=` followed by 8+ chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]; `apiKey=`, `KEY=`, `key=` with shorter tokens, or tokens containing `.`, `+`, `/`, `%` are missed or only partly masked (the tail after the first non-class char stays in the output).
findings.effect: A key written in a different case or with punctuation in a fetched gradle/catalog/state file is published in the HTML and JSON dashboard instead of being masked.

findings.summary: subprocess.run for every gh api call has no timeout, and collect() waits on all futures (build.py:319, 330) so one stalled gh process blocks the whole thread pool join indefinitely
findings.effect: A regeneration can hang forever on a stalled network or auth prompt instead of failing, exceeding the 30 minute budget with no error.

findings.summary: in_scope rebuilds set(self.team_paths(team)) and scans all rules on every call, and build.in_scope_modules calls it once per module directory, so the invariant set is recomputed inside the loop
findings.effect: none: only a small CPU cost during generation, a few hundred modules times a few hundred rules.

findings.summary: AcceptanceTest/Generated.setUp calls self.fail unless out/data.json and out/dashboard.html already exist from a separate live gh run, so ~15 acceptance tests error on any clean checkout or CI and a plain `unittest` run is red without network and gh auth.
findings.effect: A developer or CI job running unittest on a clean checkout sees 14 of 16 acceptance tests fail until a live gh-authenticated generator run has produced out/; the shipped dashboard itself does not change.
findings.evidence: tests/test_acceptance.py:37-38 calls self.fail when out/data.json or out/dashboard.html is absent; out/ is gitignored (.gitignore:1), so a clean checkout of HEAD has neither file and the acceptance suite fails. Lead claim survives (no merged claims). Damage is test-only: the dashboard and generator are unaffected.

repro.cmd: git archive HEAD | tar -x -C scratchpad/clone && cd scratchpad/clone && python3 -m unittest tests.test_acceptance

findings.summary: Hard-coded date-pinned live values (LATEST_STABLE 2.4.5, LATEST_RC 2.8.0-rc01, behind_rc == 12, the 26 reference pairs) make tests fail on the next go-sdk-android release even though the generator is correct, so a failure does not signal a regression.

The collect() branch raising RuntimeError when a consumer catalog is missing (text is None), and github.tree()'s truncated-tree RuntimeError, have no test; deleting either check leaves the suite green and a missing catalog would silently flow on.
Comment says RECON_TAGS runs 'from 2.6.0 up to 2.8.0-rc01' but the list also contains 2.4.5, 2.5.6 and 2.5.7, which are older than 2.6.0.

The change adds a CLI and a unittest suite but README.md (which documents what/build/validate) is not updated; the only run instructions live in the __main__ and test_acceptance docstrings, and the acceptance test fails until a live run was done.

security.focus: Five categories, each walked on every changed file: secrets or credentials reaching a log, an error message or a caller; injection at a trust boundary (shell, SQL, path, template); unsafe deserialization or evaluation; a new entry point that skips a check its siblings make; dependency risk introduced by this change.
checked: secrets: traced redact.py through github.raw, __main__ output writes, html.render; grep of repo for key/token/secret found only the redact tests and ACCEPTANCE.md M5 (no committed secrets)

injection: github.py _gh uses an argv list with no shell, endpoints start with repos/; __main__ os.path.join uses module dirs from git tree paths (git forbids .. components); html.py escapes every interpolated value with _e
deserialization: only tomllib.loads and json.loads of gh output are used; no eval, pickle or yaml load anywhere in generator/
entry points: __main__.py is the only CLI and it routes all fetches through github.py GET-only helpers; --extra-catalog reads a local path the operator supplies and redacts it
dependencies: generator imports stdlib only; no manifest or lockfile added; gh binary resolved from PATH

performance.focus: Algorithmic complexity on a hot path, blocking I/O where the surroundings are asynchronous, unbounded growth of a collection or buffer, repeated work inside a loop that could run once.
